verdict.rationale: Semgrep Code is documented as a SAST tool whose rules use pattern matching and data-flow analysis to find security issues. Its taint tracking is explicitly described as catching complex injection bugs such as XSS, and cross-file analysis extends detection across files. Community users corroborate its use for security lint rules and curated per-language rules, though one hands-on report notes a simple exec pattern search missed an aliasing workaround. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that the out-of-the-box rulesets cover injection/XSS classes (the taint docs frame it as writing your own rules), and evidence that aliasing-style evasions are handled.

support.subject: As a developer, I can run static analysis that finds vulnerability classes like injection and XSS in my source code

citations.quote: Taint tracking (known also as taint analysis) enables you to write simple rules that catch complex injection bugs, such as those that can result in cross-site scripting (XSS).
Semgrep Code is a static application security testing (SAST) tool that
Semgrep uses rules, which encapsulate pattern matching logic and data flow analysis, to scan your code for security issues, style violations, bugs, and more.
To turn on cross-file analysis, which allows you to detect vulnerabilities across files and folders
